children.value: > Fact From Story: “They’re overdoing it a little bit, for sure,” Kelce agreed.

> > Fact From Story: In conversation with his brother Jason, 35, the two addressed concerns from longtime football enthusiasts who were frustrated by the constant Swift references throughout Sunday’s game at MetLife Stadium.
> > > Fact From Story: Travis Kelce believes the National Football League’s coverage of his rumoured girlfriend Taylor Swift is a bit too much.
> > > Commonsense Knowledge: If someone agrees that something is too much, then they believe that thing is too much.
> > Fact From Story: Travis Kelce believes the National Football League’s coverage of his rumoured girlfriend Taylor Swift is a bit too much.
> > Commonsense Knowledge: If someone agrees that something is too much, then they believe that thing is too much.

> Fact From Story: Not only did the football league promote last Sunday’s game by speculating whether the Grammy winner will attend the Chiefs-Jets match, but cameras were constantly panning to the star-studded suite.
> > Fact From Story: The NFL also introduced a special segment with Carson Daly and The Voice, where the famed host attempted to explain the specifics of football to “Swifties.”

> > > Fact From Story: During the game, Swift was joined an A-list group of guests, including her best friends Blake Lively and Ryan Reynolds, Game of Thrones star Sophie Turner, and actor Hugh Jackman.
> > > Commonsense Knowledge: Having many famous people attend an event implies the event is important.

> > Fact From Story: During the game, Swift was joined an A-list group of guests, including her best friends Blake Lively and Ryan Reynolds, Game of Thrones star Sophie Turner, and actor Hugh Jackman.
> > > Fact From Story: The NFL also introduced a special segment with Carson Daly and The Voice, where the famed host attempted to explain the specifics of football to “Swifties.”
> > > Commonsense Knowledge: Explaining a sport to a specific group implies an attempt to attract that group to the sport.
> > Commonsense Knowledge: Promoting an event and showing it often implies the event is receiving a lot of coverage.
> Commonsense Knowledge: If someone says something is "overdoing it", they are saying it is too much.
